title: UNETR: Transformers for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
layout_note: Transformer encoder is a single vertical column on the far left (top to bottom); four token outputs (z3, z6, z9, z12) leave it as horizontal rails at evenly spaced heights, and the CNN decoder climbs back up as a diagonal staircase from bottom-centre to top-right, merging one rail per step. The deepest rail (z12) enters at the bottom, the full-resolution input skip runs along the very top.
grouping: The repeated transformer layer sits in one light-grey background panel marked 'x12', with its residual connections drawn as lines looping around the panel edge; Linear Projection and Embedded Patches are separate tinted bars stacked above the panel. The decoder is grouped only by block colour families (one colour per operation type), explained in a framed legend box in the bottom-right corner; there are no containers around encoder or decoder stages.
shapes_depth: Two drawing registers: the transformer internals (Norm, Multi-Head Attention, MLP, projection bars) are flat square-cornered rectangles with no shadow, while every convolution/deconvolution block is an extruded 3-D cuboid with lighter top and darker side faces, placed in short runs of 1-3 touching cubes. Concatenation is a small filled circle with 'C'; residual addition is an outlined circle with '+'. Input and output are square MRI slice thumbnails, the input shown as a small stack of offset slices. Thin black orthogonal arrows connect everything.
proposed_highlight: No module is named on the canvas beyond the plain layer labels; the method is carried by the drawing itself: the transformer block is set apart by its grey panel and flat style, and decoder operations are distinguished only by cube colour keyed to the legend (deconv, deconv+conv+BN+ReLU, conv+BN+ReLU, 1x1x1 conv). Italic z-labels name each extracted encoder layer at the start of its rail.
lesson: Pull skip features out of a vertical encoder column as horizontal rails at evenly spaced heights and let the decoder climb a diagonal staircase back up, so every merge node sits at the height of the rail it consumes and its tensor size is written just under it.
notes: Venue from arXiv journal-ref; year 2022 verified from the arXiv comment ('Accepted to WACV 2022'). Every arrow segment carries a tensor-size label set as a stacked fraction (H/16 x W/16 x D/16 x 768 etc.), so resolution change along the staircase is readable without a scale bar. Legend uses the same 3-D cubes as the canvas rather than flat swatches.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

insights.structure: The transformer encoder is one vertical grey column at the far left; tokens z3, z6, z9, z12 leave it as horizontal rails at even heights and the CNN decoder climbs as a diagonal staircase to the top right, merging one rail per step at blue C nodes.
insights.data: Convolution blocks are coloured 3-D cuboids in short runs (blue, yellow, green, grey by operation) with tensor shapes like H/16 x W/16 x D/16 x 768 typeset under each rail; the input and output are real brain MRI slices, the output with a red overlay.
insights.emphasis: The rails from evenly spaced transformer layers make the 'skip from transformer depth' idea the dominant visual; the decoder staircase is the only diagonal element.
insights.flow: Input top-left goes down the encoder column; rails run right; the decoder rises bottom-centre to top-right ending at the output at upper right.
insights.avoid: Transformer internals are flat square boxes while decoder blocks are 3-D cuboids, two unrelated drawing registers in one figure; the legend box takes a large bottom-right area.

arrangement.units: one composition: grey encoder panel (x12) at left, unframed decoder staircase; framed legend box
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real MRI slices at top-left
